comparator.name: Criminology
comparator.sourceNotes: The live Leiden Study Guide product confirms a current 180-EC Criminology bachelor and supplies the revised first and second years in full. Each contains twelve compulsory 5-EC modules, together establishing 120 EC in criminology, law, criminal justice, psychology, sociology, qualitative and quantitative research, policy evaluation, victims, offenders, cybercrime, investigation, prosecution and experiments. The same product explicitly states that its displayed third year is the old curriculum for students who began in 2024 or earlier and that Year 3 of the revised curriculum will first be included in the 2027-2028 Study Guide. Because a Fall 2026 entrant cannot combine the revised Years 1-2 with that legacy Year 3, only the supported 120 EC of the applicable revised curriculum are retained. The zero-credit Language Test Criminology, Tutoring/LLP Criminology and Leiden Law Practices entries are noted in the official product but omitted from the positive-credit component list.

exception.reason: Leiden is phasing in a revised Criminology curriculum. The current 2026-2027 Study Guide establishes the revised first and second years, but it expressly labels the displayed third year as the old curriculum for students who began in 2024 or earlier and states that Year 3 of the revised curriculum will only be published in the 2027-2028 guide. Combining the 120 EC revised sequence with the 60 EC legacy third year would create a pathway that no Fall 2026 entrant can follow. The missing applicable third-year structure cannot be inferred from the outgoing curriculum without inventing compulsory, elective, research and thesis requirements.
exception.curriculumContext: The applicable revised curriculum is supported for 120 EC: 60 EC in Year 1 and 60 EC in Year 2, each composed of twelve compulsory 5-EC modules. It establishes integrated criminological theory, legal and criminal-justice study, psychological and sociological explanations, qualitative and quantitative methods, professional skills, policy evaluation, victims and offenders, cybercrime, investigation and prosecution, forensic psychology and experimental methods. The current product confirms that the programme as a whole is 180 EC, but the remaining revised 60 EC are not yet published. The legacy Year 3 shown in the same product is deliberately excluded because Leiden restricts it to earlier cohorts.
